A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VideoPASTA research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved between sections.

before.justification: V2 reports original evaluations of VideoPASTA-trained models, preference-generation ablations, smaller-model experiments and adversarial robustness results.

after.justification: V3 retains these original experiments and adds MovieChat/EgoSchema evaluations and an MVBench subtask breakdown.

M1.justification: The adversarial generation, filtering and weighted DPO procedure remain unchanged. Section 3 clarifies that adversarial queries generate rejected responses while training uses the original aligned query; this is consistent with v2's Figure 2 and unchanged prompt templates, rather than a new method component.

E1.justification: V3 adds supplementary evaluation on MovieChat and EgoSchema, extending coverage of movie and egocentric videos. ActivityNet training and the original seven benchmarks remain. The new MVBench breakdown reports tasks within an already evaluated benchmark.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same foundation models, SFT, Hound-DPO, TPO and off-the-shelf comparators. The added domain and subtask evaluations reuse existing foundation-model baselines without changing comparator membership in retained experiments.

E3.justification: The data-quality evaluation changes its reported sample from 200 preference pairs containing three adversarial examples each in v2 Appendix A.1 to 200 adversarial examples in v3 Section 4.2. This changes the stated sampling protocol, although unchanged accuracies do not establish that the experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: V3 adds a domain-transfer check and an MVBench action/attribute analysis examining whether reasoning alignment also benefits perception (Tables 4–5). Existing component ablations, robustness tests, hyperparameter studies and qualitative examples remain. Failure-mode targeting accuracy is relocated from the appendix, not newly introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or comparable uncertainty estimates. The added results continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes InternVL2.5 + VideoPASTA's LongVideoBench result from 56.7 (+3.8) to 58.1 (+5.2), without explaining the revision or stating changed settings. New Tables 4–5 report MovieChat/EgoSchema gains up to 1.9/1.6 percentage points and improvements on eight of nine MVBench subtasks, including +12.0 for Action Localization and -0.5 for Action Prediction. Other matched numerical tables retain their results.

T1.justification: The preference-data definitions, DPO objective and dataset-count calculations in Equations 1–4 are mathematically unchanged. Neither version adds formal assumptions, theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central claims of model-agnostic alignment using 7,020 targeted preference pairs without human annotation or captioning. Percentage-point wording clarifies existing absolute gains; the main contribution and headline seven-benchmark claims are not redefined.

C2.justification: V3 adds interpretations linking targeted reasoning alignment to domain transfer and lower-level perception, and makes the self-correction-versus-distillation argument explicit. It removes v2's explanation attributing lower cross-frame targeting accuracy to continuity complexity. The limitations paragraph remains unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 3 explicitly documents which query accompanies rejected responses during training. The shortened data-quality description omits v2's statement about concealing the intended failure category from the judge. Hardware, hyperparameters, prompt templates and project-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V3 adds references to AVATAR, MovieChat and EgoSchema. It removes CoS/Chain-of-Shot and substitutes the existing hallucination-survey citation in the training-free-methods passage. Other prominent citation changes are publication updates, while the overall positioning against existing alignment approaches remains stable.

P1.justification: V3 locally rewrites the method overview and experimental rationale, clarifies percentage-point terminology, moves and condenses preference-quality analysis into Section 4.2, renames the dataset-example subsection and adds acknowledgments. The broader narrative and section organization remain recognizable.

P2.justification: V3 adds two tables, moves the existing targeting-accuracy table into the main text, standardizes several tables' gain/loss notation to plus/minus signs and adjusts captions and layout. Existing figures and illustrated examples are retained without substantive graphical replacement.

improvement.justification: The added domain evaluations and MVBench diagnostics provide focused empirical support that v2 lacked, while the query-handling explanation and percentage-point wording improve clarity. These benefits are limited by sparse documentation of the new evaluations, the changed quality-check sampling description, and a new inconsistency: Table 1 reports a +5.2 LongVideoBench gain while the abstract still states a maximum of +3.8.
